claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree T and natural p with x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, the complete sum S(T,p) over the fixed original-leaf selector F(T,p) is nonpositive.
claims.scope: Exact primary lower-region contract; original supports and closed neighborhoods, zero-extended independence counts, and distinct tags for every original leaf are retained.
claims.reason: The selected aggregate is exactly a difference of adjacent ranks of a fixed-selector weighted independent-set count, and an explicit cross-tag deletion transport would suffice. Its required tree-specific capacity inequality is not proved, and no eligible positive full-sum tree is exhibited.

limitations: The proposed cross-tag Hall or fractional-flow capacity inequality has not been proved under the favorable-selector and lower-region hypotheses.
The rank-weight reformulation is not a sign argument; no full-sum counterexample or universal proof is supplied.
No finite census or external theorem is used as evidence for a universal conclusion.
